risk_if_not_implemented: Without Terminating Third-Party Relationships, the organization may be unable to disengage from a third party in an orderly way, leaving it dependent on a provider that is failing, insolvent, non-compliant or no longer needed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), Third-Party Dependency Failure (R-SC-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency (MT-24).

compensating_control_1.name: Break Clauses
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to include "break clauses" within contracts for failure to meet contract criteria for security, compliance and/or resilience controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Break Clauses (TPM-19) compensates for the absence of Terminating Third-Party Relationships (TPM-24) by embedding contractual break clauses that preserve the organization's right to exit under defined conditions, which supplies the legal basis an exit strategy would otherwise formalize. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Supplier Diversity
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to obtain security, compliance and resilience technologies from different suppliers to minimize supply chain risk.
compensating_control_2.justification: Supplier Diversity (TPM-06) compensates for the absence of Terminating Third-Party Relationships (TPM-24) by maintaining alternative suppliers for security, compliance and resilience technologies, which reduces the concentration risk and dependency failure that make an unplanned exit damaging. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
